name: Fremont
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Fremont, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Fremont, CA: tree lightings, Santa at Pacific Commons and the library, Victorian tours at Ardenwood and the Niles lights.
lede: Fremont celebrates Christmas district by district: a lighted parade in historic Niles, tree lightings downtown and at Pacific Commons, Victorian holiday tours at Ardenwood and a neighborhood lights tradition that dates to 1967.
celebrates: The season starts the Friday after Thanksgiving in Niles, where the Niles Main Street Association lights the tree and sends the Festival of Lights Parade down Niles Boulevard. Shopping centers follow with their own trees: Pacific Commons holds a celebration with Santa, and Fremont Hub fills its courtyard with faux snow. Downtown, the City of Fremont hosts Holidays at the Plaza with a tree lighting, hot chocolate and cookie decorating. At Ardenwood Historic Farm, docents in period dress lead tours of the decorated Patterson House, and in the Westridge neighborhood the Crippsmas Club lights up the streets around Nicolet Avenue every December.
lastyear: In 2025 the Niles Festival of Lights Parade ran on Friday, November 28, with a tree lighting at 6 pm and 60 floats in the parade that followed. Pacific Commons held its celebration the next day with photos with Santa, face painting and train rides. On Friday, December 5, the city held its second Holidays at the Plaza at 3500 Capitol Avenue, with food trucks, cookie decorating and a holiday market, and the Tri-City Voice noted that the Grinch came instead of Santa.
facts: Niles has held its Festival of Lights Parade since 2001, and the merchants who started it still run it through the Niles Main Street Association, paid for entirely by sponsors. The parade draws more than 10,000 spectators along a half-mile route. Crippsmas Place has been decorating its neighborhood since 1967, and its volunteers hand out candy canes and collect donations for local charities. The Patterson House at Ardenwood began as a farmhouse built in 1857 and gained its Queen Anne addition in 1889.
trains: Fremont is a railroad town at heart. Niles grew up in the 1850s as a junction where Southern Pacific lines from Oakland met the routes to San Jose and the coast. Today Amtrak's Capitol Corridor stops at Fremont-Centerville, and BART serves the Fremont and Warm Springs/South Fremont stations. Each holiday season the Niles Canyon Railway runs its Train of Lights, a 1.5 hour round trip through Niles Canyon in decorated antique coaches, with one departure from Niles at dusk and another from Sunol after dark.

The City of Fremont lights a big tree at the Downtown Event Center and adds hot chocolate, food trucks and gingerbread cookie decorating.

Costumed docents lead tours through 14 rooms decorated for a turn of the 20th century Christmas at Ardenwood Historic Farm.
Neighbors in the Westridge area have decorated their streets since 1967, and families stroll or drive through each December.

kidfact: Long ago, Niles was a busy train junction where railroad lines from Oakland met the tracks to San Jose. Every Christmas, a train covered in lights still rolls through Niles Canyon.
faq: When is the Niles Festival of Lights Parade?

The Niles Festival of Lights Parade is always on the Friday after Thanksgiving. The Niles Main Street Association lights the tree at Niles Town Plaza at 6 pm, and the parade follows along Niles Boulevard. The organizers say the parade draws more than 10,000 spectators along its half-mile route, and chairs may not be set out until noon that day.
What is Crippsmas Place in Fremont?

Crippsmas Place is a neighborhood holiday display in Fremont's Westridge area, along Nicolet Avenue and the surrounding streets, that has run since 1967. The Crippsmas Club organizes it, and families can walk the sidewalks or drive through to see the lights. Volunteers hand out candy canes and collect donations for local charities.
Where can kids see Santa in Fremont?

Santa appears at the Pacific Commons holiday celebration and tree lighting, at the Holiday Snow Magic evening at Fremont Hub and at the Fremont Main Library, which holds free photos with Santa. In Niles, Santa rides in the Festival of Lights Parade. Check each event on this page for this year's dates and times.
Does Fremont have a Christmas train?

Yes. The Niles Canyon Railway's Train of Lights is a holiday tradition for many Bay Area families. It is a 1.5 hour round trip through Niles Canyon in antique coaches and open cars decorated with lights, with refreshments and music. One departure leaves Niles at dusk and a second leaves Sunol after dark. The railroad is an all-volunteer, nonprofit museum, and the Train of Lights is its largest fundraiser.
How do I get to Fremont by train?

Amtrak's Capitol Corridor stops at the Fremont-Centerville station, and BART runs to the Fremont and Warm Springs/South Fremont stations. Niles itself grew up in the 1850s as a railroad junction, which is why the Niles Canyon Railway still runs holiday trains from there.
